words.sense: art of using language effectively to persuade in speech or writing
words.connotation: can be admiring or critical of persuasion
misconceptions: Assuming any speech skill is primarily persuasion by wording.

words.sense: art and style of delivering formal speeches to audiences
words.connotation: usually formal and associated with speaking skill
misconceptions: Assuming all persuasive language is public speaking.
Mistaking polished writing for speech delivery.

semantic_axes.description: Rhetoric concerns how words persuade in speech or writing, whereas oratory specifically concerns skilled formal public speaking.

edges.boundary_rule: Rhetoric concerns how words persuade in speech or writing, whereas oratory specifically concerns skilled formal public speaking.

misconceptions.M1: Assuming all persuasive language is public speaking.
misconceptions.M2: Mistaking polished writing for speech delivery.
misconceptions.M3: Assuming any speech skill is primarily persuasion by wording.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Zara's work on the school appeal?

beats.text: Zara rewrites a printed funding appeal to lead with a question that makes readers consider what students will lose.
beats.decisive_clue: she arranges written words to persuade readers
beats.reason: She arranges written words to persuade readers is the evidence for rhetoric.

beats.text: She also rearranges the arguments so each answer leads into the next.
beats.decisive_clue: the written argument is shaped to change readers’ minds
beats.reason: The new structure strengthens the persuasive written appeal without making it a speech performance.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: the written argument is shaped to change readers’ minds.
chains.feedback_deep: Rhetoric is effective persuasive language in writing or speech. Zara is crafting the written case, not delivering a formal address.
chains.contrast_rule: Rhetoric persuades through language; oratory commands a live audience.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Ravi's strength at graduation?

beats.text: Ravi addresses the hall, adjusting his pauses and volume until even people at the back follow him.
beats.decisive_clue: his skill appears in formal public delivery
beats.reason: His skill appears in formal public delivery is the evidence for oratory.

beats.text: He holds the microphone lower and projects his voice without rushing.
beats.decisive_clue: his controlled live delivery remains decisive
beats.reason: Moving the microphone does not turn the speaking performance into a written persuasive technique.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: his skill appears in formal public delivery.
chains.feedback_deep: Oratory focuses on the art and style of formal speech delivery. Ravi’s voice, pacing, and audience control are decisive; rhetoric could describe particular persuasive wording, which is not the focus.
chains.contrast_rule: Rhetoric persuades through language; oratory commands a live audience.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Hana's contribution to the petition?

beats.text: Hana replaces a list of complaints with a short written appeal that anticipates the landlord’s objections.
beats.decisive_clue: she crafts a written argument for persuasion
beats.reason: She crafts a written argument for persuasion is the evidence for rhetoric.

beats.text: Her last paragraph offers a practical solution before asking for signatures.
beats.reason: The practical solution supports the same written persuasive strategy rather than turning it into public speech.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: she crafts a written argument for persuasion.
chains.feedback_deep: Rhetoric includes persuasive writing. Hana’s language is organized to overcome objections; there is no formal speech delivery to evaluate.
chains.contrast_rule: Rhetoric persuades through language; oratory commands a live audience.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Pablo's talent at the awards night?

beats.text: Pablo gives a formal address, holding a crowded room through changes in pitch and a carefully timed pause.
beats.decisive_clue: his formal address is carried by live delivery
beats.reason: His formal address is carried by live delivery is the evidence for oratory.

beats.text: He speaks without looking down at his notes even when the lights dim.
beats.decisive_clue: his delivery skill remains the main evidence
beats.reason: Not needing notes is an extra performance detail; the main distinction remains formal public speaking.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: his formal address is carried by live delivery.
chains.feedback_deep: The evidence concerns Pablo’s command of a live formal address. That is oratory; the lighting and notes do not turn the task into constructing a persuasive argument.
chains.contrast_rule: Rhetoric persuades through language; oratory commands a live audience.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Samira's technique in her donation post?

beats.text: Samira writes, “For the price of one snack, a child can have a book,” to make a small gift feel possible.
beats.decisive_clue: her written comparison is designed to persuade
beats.reason: Her written comparison is designed to persuade is the evidence for rhetoric.

beats.text: Her post reaches readers who have never heard of the charity before.
beats.decisive_clue: her comparison makes giving feel achievable to new readers
beats.reason: The audience widens, but the skill remains a persuasive written comparison.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: her comparison makes giving feel achievable to new readers.
chains.feedback_deep: Rhetoric includes framing an appeal so readers rethink an action. Samira’s comparison works in text without relying on a formal public performance.
chains.contrast_rule: Rhetoric persuades through language; oratory commands a live audience.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Elias's ability during his election speech?

beats.text: Elias stands before the year group and carries his speech with clear projection, rhythm and deliberate silence.
beats.decisive_clue: the strength is formal spoken delivery
beats.reason: The strength is formal spoken delivery is the evidence for oratory.

beats.text: He slows at the difficult section so everyone can hear each point.
beats.decisive_clue: he controls pace to sustain audience attention
beats.reason: Slowing the speech adds evidence about the quality of the live performance.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: he controls pace to sustain audience attention.
chains.feedback_deep: Oratory is skilled formal public speaking. Elias’s pacing and projection distinguish it from rhetoric, which would focus on persuasive language choices.
chains.contrast_rule: Rhetoric persuades through language; oratory commands a live audience.
